me_2_four_seasons_crag.blurb: A hidden woodland cliff among the Chain of Ponds crags in western Maine, tucked in the trees a short climb above the highway. It holds ten single-pitch lines, nearly all trad plus one sport route, mostly in the 5.7 to 5.8 range with a handful of harder leads up to 5.12. The granite faces south, but the dense forest keeps the air still and the rock slow to dry after rain, and the middle of the face stays wet. Some routes have no lower-off, so leaders top out and walk or rappel down. In winter the same wall grows several short ice lines, and a small bouldering band sits up and left of the main face.

me_geo_cache_boulder.blurb: The first boulder you meet on arriving at The Spot, a bouldering zone above the Guide Wall in Camden Hills State Park. Ten problems share one steep wall of roughly 45 degrees, with good landings, plus a low block to the right that offers a few easier lines. Grades run from V0 up through V2 for the gentle end, then a few mid-grade problems at V5 and V6, and several V8 lines including a pair of projects. The Spot sits on grippy, sometimes sharp gneiss. Expect a steep scramble up a gully and goat path to get there, so it suits climbers happy to hike with pads.

me_parking_lot_boulders.blurb: A cluster of seaside boulders just below the parking area at the Nubble Lighthouse on Maine's southern coast. You walk toward the water to reach them, and there are ten problems with a spread from V0 to a hard project. Most sit between V0 and V6, with a run of V5 problems at the upper end. Landings near the sea can be wet and slippery, and the area is best enjoyed around low tide, so bring pads and a spotter. Topouts are generally short and solid. Some lines take a little searching to find, and the setting is busy with visitors to the lighthouse.

me_mcclellan_park.blurb: A small bouldering spot on the rocky shoreline of McClellan Park in Maine's Downeast region, near Milbridge. Ten problems are spread over two main rocks, Shoreline Boulder and Lava Rock Boulder. Most lines are V1 to V3, with a few harder ones up to around V5. The boulders are short, about ten feet, so anything above the easy grades tends to begin with a low or cramped start, and topouts are solid. Shoreline Boulder offers the crimpier, more intense lines while Lava Rock Boulder suits a warm-up. The ocean breeze keeps summer days cooler. Fun for a stop, though not a destination by itself.

me_family_wall_the.blurb: A steep slab about 80 feet tall at Shell Pond, in the Evans Notch area of western Maine near the New Hampshire line. The wall carries ten trad and sport lines, mostly from easy fifth class up through 5.9 and 5.10, with one at the 5.2 level and a handful of moderates that suit newer leaders. It is the first cliff reached on the pond trail from the Deer Hill side, and the top is an open bluff with a view over the water. Visits are light, so some routes are mossy and could use a brush. A 60-meter rope reaches the top trees for top-roping, and the walk-off is down a trail on climbers' left.
